transcript.content: Hi, welcome in — I'm Dr. Lee. What brings you in to see me today?

Um… well, I guess the main thing is work. I’ve been having a hard time keeping track of things I’m supposed to follow up on — callbacks, work orders, stuff I told people I’d check on and get back to them about. I don’t mean to drop the ball, but it keeps happening, and it’s kind of piled up.

My supervisor… they suggested I come in before it gets any worse, especially because I was hoping to move up. I’m not trying to make excuses, I just… I need to figure out why I can’t seem to stay on top of these things like I should.
Thinking back, when did you first start noticing this kind of trouble keeping track of tasks and follow-ups — has it been a lifelong pattern, or did it start more recently?

I think… it’s been there a long time, honestly. I don’t want to make it sound like I was a terrible student or anything — I did okay, and teachers would say I was bright — but even back in grade school I was always misplacing papers or not catching all the directions.

I remember needing reminders to finish classwork, things like that. So… yeah, I guess it didn’t just start with this job. The work pressure is just making it harder to hide, maybe.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you noticed any changes in your mood—like feeling down, losing interest in things you usually enjoy, or feeling low on energy?

Um… I don’t think so? Not in a big way, anyway. I mean, I get frustrated with myself, especially when I mess something up at work, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been, like, down all the time or not enjoying things.

Energy’s… maybe normal for me? I’m not sure. I don’t think there’s been some major change these past couple weeks. Does that answer it okay?
Do you often feel restless, fidgety, or have trouble sitting still, or find yourself acting or speaking impulsively without thinking it through?

Um… not really, I don’t think. I mean, I’ll tap my foot sometimes or shift around if I’m sitting too long, but I don’t think people would say I’m, like, bouncing off the walls or interrupting all the time.

Impulsive speaking… maybe once in a while like anyone, but I try pretty hard not to. I’m not sure if that’s what you mean. Does that sound like what you’re asking?
Do you notice similar problems with forgetfulness, losing track of tasks, or disorganization in other areas of your life outside of work—like at home, with personal errands, or in relationships?

Yeah… I mean, I wish I could say it was only work, but it does kind of spill over. The thing that really brought me in, though, is at work I keep forgetting scheduled callbacks, work orders, and basic follow-ups I told people I’d do.

I try to write things down, and I’m not trying to be careless, but it’s piled up enough that they sent me here before I lose my chance at moving up. So… it’s not like I’m ignoring people on purpose. I just lose track, and then I feel awful about it.
Do you often find it hard to keep your attention focused during tasks or activities, like reading, meetings, or lengthy work orders, even when you're trying to concentrate?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I try to pay attention, especially with the work orders, because I know they matter. But I’ll start reading one on the tablet thinking, okay, I’ve got this, and then halfway through the notes my mind just kind of… slips off. Like I’ll hear something nearby or think about the next job, and then I realize I don’t actually know what I just read.

It’s embarrassing, because it’s not that I don’t care. I really am trying. I usually have to go back and reread it, sometimes more than once. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you often lose or misplace things you need for daily tasks—like your keys, wallet, phone, or paperwork—at home or elsewhere?

Yeah… I do. I mean, I try to keep my stuff in the same place, so it doesn’t sound like I’m just being sloppy, but I’m constantly hunting for things.

At work it’s the tablet, keys, my flashlight, or even a tool I literally just had in my hand a minute ago. I’ll set it down “just for a second,” and then I can’t find it. And then I’m holding up the job or walking back and forth looking for it, which… honestly makes me look careless, even though I’m really not trying to be. Does that make sense?
Do you find yourself worrying a lot, more than most people, about things going wrong or not getting done, to the point that it's hard to relax or shut your mind off?

I don’t know… I mean, I worry some, sure, especially when I know I’ve got things I’m supposed to do. But I’m not sure I’d say it’s more than most people, or that I can’t relax at all.

It’s more like… if something is hanging over me, I’ll think about it, but I don’t know if that’s unusual. Am I answering that right?
Have you noticed any problems with your sleep—like trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or feeling rested—or do you use alcohol, caffeine, or other substances that might affect your concentration?

Um… I’m not really sure. I mean, I sleep, I guess. I haven’t really tracked it or anything, so I don’t want to say there’s a big problem if there isn’t.

I do have caffeine sometimes, like most people, but I don’t know that it’s affecting my concentration. And substances… no, nothing I can think of that would be relevant. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking?

Thinking back to before you were about 12 years old, do you remember having noticeable trouble paying attention in class, finishing schoolwork, or keeping track of your things—beyond what would be typical for kids your age?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it was, because I did okay in some ways, but I do remember being like this even in grade school.

Teachers would say I was bright, but I’d miss parts of the directions or not finish the classwork unless someone reminded me. And I was always losing papers or not knowing where I put things. So… yeah, it wasn’t just something that started with work stress now. Does that answer what you mean?
